clue.text: Occurred to little shop girl a month back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the assembled pieces from right to left

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop
FEB is the short form of February

explanation.surface: Something has happened to a young shop assistant about a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little shop girl' is not a junior assistant but Little Nell, the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop; 'back' turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: To befall is to happen to someone, so the past participle matches the phrase 'occurred to'.

clue.text: "Stop it!" Youngsters do show shame

indicators.note: the words do show what lies inside them, signalling letters concealed across the run of the clue

explanation.surface: An adult tells children to stop misbehaving because they are disgracing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'stoP IT Youngsters', spanning the end of the quoted command and the start of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'what a shame' the word means a regrettable thing, a synonym for the answer as in 'what a pity'.

clue.text: Basic accommodation in Black Country

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the other one

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it
a hut is simple, rough shelter

explanation.surface: A spartan place to stay in the Black Country, the industrial West Midlands area of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Country' looks like the English region (the industrial West Midlands); 'Black' is BAN, as in to black goods, and 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom is an example of a country.

clue.text: Son isn't a planned outcome of their actions

definitions.text: Son isn't a planned outcome of their actions

indicators.note: planned suggests the letters are arranged to a new design

explanation.surface: A wry remark that certain people's activities are never meant to produce a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges the letters of SON ISNT A; read whole, the clue also describes the practice: no son can come of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Masturbators engage in a solitary practice that cannot produce children, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Passing on hawk-like ring

parts.note: a hawk in politics is pro-war, i.e. for war
a ding is the ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A predator's circling flight, or a bird-of-prey's style of ring, is handed along.
explanation.walkthrough: A hawk in politics favours military action, so 'hawk-like' is FOR WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Forwarding a letter or message is sending it on to someone else.

clue.text: Left in charge, teenager's opening wine

indicators.note: in puts the first-named letter inside the following word

parts.note: something in your charge is in your care

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A teenager is left in charge and starts with a bottle of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside CARE to give CLARE; 'opening' takes the T of teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a type of wine.

clue.text: Each one discarded went off

parts.note: per means for each, as in five pounds per head
the Roman numeral for one is I
to shed something is to cast it off

explanation.surface: Each item was thrown away because it had gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off has spoilt or decayed, which is what rubber or food does when it perishes.

clue.text: Steep's a top actress (need to add an "r")

indicators.note: an extra letter must be put into the actress's name

parts.note: Dame Judi Dench is a leading British actress

explanation.surface: A note about spelling a famous actress's name, wrapped round a word about soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep's' is 'Steep is'; 'need to add' puts R into DENCH, the surname of Dame Judi Dench.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it thoroughly in liquid, a synonym for soaking through.

clue.text: Fool head? One may be in the soup

definitions.meaning: informal word for the skull or brain

definitions.text: One may be in the soup
definitions.meaning: a strip of pasta, found in chicken soup

explanation.surface: Calling someone a fool and a blockhead, with a nod to being in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; 'in the soup' also suggests being in trouble, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fool, slang for the head, and a strip of pasta served in soup.

clue.text: Emma's young fellow's hot … mainly after exercise!

parts.note: a lad is a boy or young man

indicators.note: the letters, once given a workout, are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A young man is all sweaty after a workout at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emma' is Emma, Lady Hamilton, not Jane Austen's heroine; 'after exercise' gives YHAMILTON from the letters of 'hot' and 'mainly' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma, Lady Hamilton, was the famous mistress of Admiral Nelson.

clue.text: Sour response from women haters — "Lena's unbalanced"

indicators.note: unbalanced suggests letters knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Misogynists cruelly dismiss a woman named Lena as mentally unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbalanced' rearranges all the letters of WOMEN HATERS and LENAS. The phrase is a dismissive reply meaning no satisfactory solution exists.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is sour, so this saying, meaning there is no good solution, is a tart reply.

clue.text: See 11
Karma — we twerk with old bird!

indicators.note: twerking is a wild gyrating dance, so the letters are shaken about

explanation.surface: A dancer announces that fate decrees we shall twerk alongside an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twerk' shakes up KARMA, WE and OLD together.
explanation.definitionFit: This American songbird is a species of lark, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Cut singers from ensemble — allocation not working

parts.note: the cast is the whole company of performers

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the next word's letters

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Singers are dropped from a group because their share of the work has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON (working) from RATION, leaving RATI.
explanation.definitionFit: These were male singers castrated before puberty to keep a high voice, hence 'cut'.

clue.text: Annoying person is lacking subtlety

indicators.note: lacking means going without the following word

parts.note: a nuisance is someone who irritates

explanation.surface: An irritating person has no finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes IS out of NUISANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning, a subtle distinction.

clue.text: Billed singers sign with John

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a lavatory
Aries the Ram is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Performers on the poster put their names on a contract with a man called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billed' means having beaks, not advertised. 'with' sets CAN beside ARIES, and the answer puts the john first.
explanation.definitionFit: These small finches have beaks and are famous for their song.

clue.text: Savings scheme — one that's good making profit, reportedly

definitions.note: profit sounds like prophet, a holy seer of the Old Testament

parts.note: an ISA is a UK tax-free Individual Savings Account
the Roman numeral for one is I
'Ah!' is an exclamation of satisfaction

explanation.surface: A savings account is touted as a good way to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account. The definition is a sound-alike: 'profit, reportedly' is prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the major Hebrew prophets, with an Old Testament book named after him.

clue.text: See 10
Nuts to break up over European Community

indicators.note: over here means one piece covers the other, holding it within
in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to snap is to break

explanation.surface: Instructions to crack nuts above some European bureaucracy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the word for break from bottom to top, giving PANS, which then sits 'over' (wrapped round) the Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecans are a kind of edible nut from North America.

clue.text: Bum, of course, wobbling — no good interfering

indicators.note: interfering means getting in among the other letters
wobbling suggests the letters are unsteady and shifted

explanation.surface: Someone's backside, naturally, is wobbling, and meddling does no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like a noun, a backside, but is the verb meaning to cadge, as in bum a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum a cigarette is to cadge or beg one, a synonym.

clue.text: Caught bird that's black and yellow

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the raven is a large all-black crow

explanation.surface: A bird with black and yellow plumage has been captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like part of the bird's colouring; it is the definition, meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means cowardly too.

clue.text: Grown-up girl's crime

parts.note: a big boy or girl is grown up
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An adult woman's offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying a second spouse while still married is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Creates endless colour in plots

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: flower beds are garden plots

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone makes endless colour in garden plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' looks like schemes, but here means garden beds.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to produce or generate, as in familiarity breeds contempt.

clue.text: Bespoke leotard? I am surprised

indicators.note: being surprised throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find their leotard was made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprised' rearranges LEOTARD and I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothes are made to an individual's order, just like made-to-measure ones.

clue.text: America's the greatest country!

parts.note: read as 'Am is', the contraction 'm as in I'm
Muhammad Ali called himself the greatest

explanation.surface: A patriotic boast that the United States is the best nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali's boast 'I am the greatest' lies behind it: the 'm of I'm plus ALI, the boxer known as the Greatest.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African state is an example of a country.

clue.text: Dish out food to audience

indicators.note: to audience means what the listeners hear, a word spoken

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.surface: A serving instruction: hand out food to the people watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to distribute or allot, as with punishment.

clue.text: Ducks in river, mostly dry

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: arid means very dry

explanation.surface: Waterfowl are on a river that has nearly run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' is the northern English endearment, not birds. 'mostly' cuts ARID to ARI, which goes 'in' DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck is a northern English term of endearment, like dear or love.

clue.text: Encouragement for revolting programme fronted by skinhead

indicators.note: fronted by puts the second piece at the front

parts.note: the head of skin is its first letter, S
an edition is one episode of a broadcast programme

explanation.surface: A TV show presented by a shaven-headed thug incites rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' is read as the head of the word skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or conduct inciting people to rebel against authority.
